M: Mom, I heard a new documentary series Our
Nature has just been released.
W: Really? That’s the one you’ve been talking about
for the past month, right?
M: Exactly! I can’t wait to watch the show about
blue whales.
W: Which channel can we watch it on?
M: Unfortunately, it’s not available on TV channels.
So I’m eager to subscribe to a new OTT service
that offers the program.
W: Do you mean it’s not included in the OTT
service we already have?
M: That’s correct, Mom.
W: Well, before subscribing to the new service, ⓐI
think you should cancel the current service first.
M: I see. I’ll think about it.

ⓐLittle people say they enjoy waiting in a long
line to buy a ticket or product. In real life, however,
people often put up with waiting in line for hours
to purchase a popular product. When a particular
fashion item, a beauty product, or a brand becomes
popular, we may feel ⓑpushing to purchase the
product to keep up with the trend. In other words,
we often choose to do something because everyone
else is doing it. The more people do something,
the more like we are to follow the act. How can
we prevent others from influencing our shopping
decisions? The next time you feel compelled to buy
a product in high demand because others do it,
first ⓒasking yourself if you really need it. Don’t be
afraid to stand out from the crowd.
Many more psychological triggers besides the
examples above will make you ⓓto spend more
money while shopping. The best way to spend
smarter is to spend after thinking carefully about
whether it is a necessary purchase, the best deal,
and the right time ⓔbuying.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞게 고쳐 쓰지못한 것은?
choices: ⓐ: Little → Few
ⓑ: pushing → pushed
ⓒ: asking → ask
ⓓ: to spend → spending
ⓔ: buying → to buy
solution: ⓓ to spend → spend

body:
We Fall Prey to Anchoring Bias
Imagine you are in a shopping center, walking by
a shoe store. A pair of striking sneakers in the
show window attracts you. At that moment, you
can hardly believe the shocking price tag: $500. Five
hundred dollars for a pair of shoes? You doubt
your own eyes and walk into the store. In the
store, you find another pair of sneakers that looks
similar for $200. After seeing the sneakers for $500,
you think the $200 sneakers are a good bargain
and buy them even though you don’t need a new
pair of sneakers. In this way, we sometimes rely too
much on __________________________________. We use it
as an anchor, or a reference point, to interpret new
information. This can lead to a hasty judgment.
How can we avoid having an anchoring bias? We
should think twice and compare prices.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: objective facts and data
desire rather than necessity
how much discount is offered
the numbers that are simply shown
the first piece of information we receive
solution: 앞에서 처음에 500달러짜리 운동화를 본 후 200달러짜리 운동 화를 보니 괜찮은 가격이라 생각한다고 했으므로, 우리가 지나 치게 의존하는 것으로 빈칸에 들어갈 것은 ❺ ‘우리가 처음으 로 접하는 정보‘가 알맞다.

“Start your free 14-day trial."
“Click here and start your free trial now.”
“Why wait? Start your trial today.”
These are typical phrases used in advertisements.
Imagine an OTT (Over the Top) media service
provider offers you a free premium service for a
month. The advertisement reassures you (A)[that /
what] you can cancel the service anytime within the
month. Marketers do this because after we use a
product, we start to feel a sense of ownership, which
(B)[make / makes] it difficult to give up the product
or switch to a different one. In other words, ⓐ우리
는 이미 우리가 소유하고 있는 상품을, 그것들이 우리
의 소유가 아니라면 우리가 할 것보다 더 과대평가하는
경향이 있다. Then, how can we overcome this
psychological ownership bias? Above all, be aware of
the “free trial” trap. Once you fall into a trap, it’s
important to remember that it can be difficult to
escape. Before you sign up for a free trial, remind
yourself about how marketers use tactics that make
you (C)[bond / boding] with their products. Cancel
the product or service if you don’t need it.

recent years. It is expected to continue to grow,
given how digitalization and the internet allow
companies to sell without a physical presence.
Factors such as convenience, a wider selection of
goods, and lower prices have contributed to the
increase in online shopping. Let’s explore the
biggest online shopping trends and see where
things are headed.
First,
more
people
will
shop
through
social
commerce. Social media and SNS services have
become increasingly popular places for consumers

Social commerce makes shopping a more convenient
and interactive experience, which helps explain why
it’s become so popular. (B) Features like “buy” buttons

choices: followbe similar to

solution: (A) 뒤에 이어지는 문장에서 우리는 다른 사람들이 모두 하고 있기 때문에 무언가를 하기로 선택한다고 했으므로, 우리가 제 품을 구매해야 할 압박감을 느끼는 이유로 트렌드를 ‘따라잡기 위해서’라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 follow(~을 따라가다), catch up with(~을 따라잡다), keep up with(~을 따라가다)가 적절하다. 간접목적어 you에 이어지는 직접목적어 역 할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다. (B) 앞 절 전체를 선행사로 부연 설명하는 계속적 용 법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 이끄는 관계사절의 동 사 자리로, 선행사가 앞 절 전체일 때 단수 취급하므 로 단수로 수일치한 makes가 적절하다. (C) 사역동사 make, 목적어 you에 이어지는 목적격보 어 자리로, 사역동사 make의 목적격보어는 목적어와 능동 관계를 이룰 때 동사원형을, 목적어와 수동 관계 를 이룰 때는 과거분사를 쓴다. 따라서 목적어 you가 ‘유대를 형성하는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 동사원 형 bond가 적절하다. 14) ①: 제품을 사용한 후에는 주인의식을 느끼게 되어 그 상품 을 포기하거나 다른 것으로 바꾸기가 어렵다고 했지만, 이는 심리적인 요인 때문일 뿐, 실제로는 무료 체험 동 안 언제든지 서비스를 취소하는 것이 가능하므로 ① ‘무료 체험 기간 동안 언제든지 서비스를 취소할 수 있 다고 말해지지만, 법적으로 불가능하다.’는 일치하지 않 는 내용이다. 오답 ② 무료 체험으로 제품을 사용한 후, 우리는 그것이 우 리에게 속해 있다고 느끼기 시작한다. ③ “무료 체험” 함정에 빠지면 벗어나기 쉽지 않다. ④ 무료 체험을 시작하기 전에, 마케터들의 전략이 우 리로 하여금 제품에 애착을 느끼게 만든다는 점을 스스 로에게 상기할 필요가 있다. ⑤ 제품이나 서비스가 필요 없다고 생각되면 그것을 취 소하는 것이 바람직하다. 15) tend to overvalue items that we already own, we would, they didn’t belong to us : • ‘~하는 경향이 있다’의 의미가 되도록 ‘tend+to부정사‘ 구문을 사용한다. • 선행사 items를 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 items 뒤에 관계대명사 that을 이어 쓰고 주어 we, 부사 already, 동사 own을 차례대로 쓴다. • ’더 높게 평가한다‘를 영작하기 위해 items that we already own 뒤에 more than을 이어 쓴다. • ’그것들이 우리의 소유가 아니라면 우리가 할 것보다‘를 영작해야 하므로, more than 뒤에 비교 대상으로 <조건> 에 맞춰 현재 사실의 반대 상황을 나타내는 가정법 과거 (주어+조동사 과거형 ~ if+주어+과거동사 …)를 사용하여 주절 we would를 먼저 쓴 후, if절에 과거동사 didn't를 사용하여 if they didn't belong to us를 이어준다. 참고로 would 뒤에는 value them이 생략되었다. 16) ⓐ While we usually believe (that) we have control over our purchasing decisions ⓑ it’s essential to understand these psychological traps that influence our spending habits. : ⓐ 동사 believe의 목적어로 완전한 절(we ~ decisions)이 이어지고 있으므로, what을 완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다. 또는 목적어절을 이끄는 접속사 that은 생략 가능하므로 생략할 수도 있다. *ⓐ에서 that은 원래 지문에서 생략되었음 ⓑ 주격 관계대명사(that)가 이끄는 절의 동사는 선행사에 수일치하는데, 선행사 these psychological traps가 복수 명사구이므로 관계사절의 동사 influences를 복수동사 influence로 고친다. 그 외, 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 to understand는 적절하다. 17) ④: 주어진 문장은 ‘앞을 내다보면, 이러한 추세는 둔화할 가능성이 낮다’라는 의미이므로, 앞부분에는 특정한 추 세가 제시되고, 뒷부분에는 그 추세가 앞으로도 계속되 거나 더욱 확대될 것임을 보여 주는 내용이 와야 한다. (D) 앞에서 2021년에 약 9,690만 명의 미국 소비자가 소셜 미디어를 통해 쇼핑을 했다는 사실이 제시되어 소셜 커머스의 성장 추세가 언급되고, (D) 뒤에서는 2025년까지 소셜 커머스 수익이 약 800억 달러에 달 하고 구매자 수가 1억 1,400만 명을 넘을 것이라는 전 망이 이어지므로 주어진 문장이 들어갈 곳으로 가장 적절한 것은 (D)이다. 18) ①: 소셜 미디어를 활용한 소셜 커머스가 편리성과 상호작 용성을 바탕으로 빠르게 성장하고 있으며, 앞으로도 이 용자가 계속 증가할 것이 글의 핵심이므로 두 번째 단 락의 요지로 적절한 것은 ① ‘소셜 커머스는 편리함과 상호작용을 제공하며 주요 쇼핑 채널로 성장하고 있다.’ 이다. 오답 ② 온라인 매장의 가격 경쟁력이 온라인 쇼핑 증가에 기여했다. ③ 온라인 쇼핑에서의 상호작용 경험은 여전히 크게 개선될 필요가 있다. ④ 소셜 커머스를 통한 쇼핑은 더 이상 강한 상승세를 보이지 않는다. ⑤ 직접 제품을 보거나 만질 수 없다는 소셜 커머스 쇼핑의 단점은 해결되어야 한다. 19) ④: 음성 비서 온라인 쇼핑의 핵심 요소가 되고 있고, 그것 을 뒷받침하는 증거로 2022년에는 400억 달러만큼의 매출에 음성 검색이 사용되었다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 2022년에는 400억 달러만큼의 매출을 This(이것)로 이 어받아 2017년의 20억 달러의 매출과 비교하여 상당한 급증이라고 언급한 (C), 두 번째로 언급한 음성 검색에 서 마지막(Finally) 전망인 인플루언서 추천으로 화제가 전환되는 (A), (A)의 마지막 문장에서 인플루언서가 마 케팅의 중요한 부분이 되고 있다는 것을 언급한 뒤 2021년에 브랜드들이 미국에서 인플루언서 마케팅 산 업에 약 37억 달러를 지출했다는 구체적인 사례를 제 시하는 (B)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 20) ③: ⓐ to get, to answer과 등위접속사 or로 병렬 연결되 어야 하므로 to call이 적절하다. ⓑ 주어는 완전한 절(people ~ searches)의 수식을 받 는 단수명사구 the way이므로 단수동사 is가 적절하다. ⓒ 완전한 절(30% of ~ decisions)에 접속사 없이 동사 가 콤마로만 이어질 수 없으므로, compare은 알맞지 않다. 부사구 또는 분사구문이 되어야 하며, 주절의 주 어 30% of consumers가 ‘비교되는’ 대상이므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 compared가 알맞다. 참고로 ‘compared to ~(~와 비교하면[비교할 때], ~에 비해)‘는 비인칭 독립분사구로, 구전치사처럼 쓰인다. 21) ④: (A) 뒤에 이어지는 문장에서 우리는 다른 사람들이 모 두 하고 있기 때문에 무언가를 하기로 선택한다고 했으 므로, 우리가 제품을 구매해야 할 압박감을 느끼는 이 유로 트렌드를 ‘따라잡기 위해서’라는 흐름이 자연스럽 다. 따라서 follow(~을 따라가다), catch up with(~을 따 라잡다), keep up with(~을 따라가다)가 적절하다. (B) 다른 사람들이 구매하기 때문에 자신도 그 제품을 구매해야 한다는 압박감을 느끼면, 먼저 그 제품이 정 말 필요한지 자신에게 물어보라고 했으므로 군중 속에 서 ‘눈에 띄는’ 것을 두려워하지 마라는 흐름이 자연스 럽다. 따라서 be distinct from(~와 구별되다), stand out from(~에서 눈에 띄다)가 적절하다. 오답 ① ~을 따라가다  ~와 비슷하다 ② ~을 따라잡다   ~와 섞이다 ③ 뒤처지다 ~와 구별되다 ⑤ 무시하다 ~와 어울리다

body:
M: Mom, I heard a new documentary series Our
Nature has just (A)[released / been released].
W: Really? That’s the one you’ve been talking about
for the past month, right?
M: Exactly! I can’t wait to watch the show about
blue whales.
W: Which channel can we watch it on?
M: Unfortunately, it’s not available on TV channels.
So I’m eager (B)[subscribing / to subscribe] to a
new OTT service that offers the program.
W: Do you mean it’s not included in the OTT
service (C)[that / what] we already have?
M: That’s correct, Mom.
W: Well, before subscribing to the new service, I
think you should cancel the current service first.
M: I see. I’ll think about it.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: been released      subscribing    that
released     to subscribe     that
been released      to subscribe     what
been released      to subscribe     that
released     subscribing    what
solution: (A) 주어 a new documentary series Our Nature에 이어지는 동사 자리이며, a new documentary series Our Nature가 ‘공 개된’ 대상이므로 조동사 has와 함께 쓰여 현재완료수동태 (have[has] been+p.p.)를 이루는 been released가 적절하다. (B) 형용사 eager는 ‘eager to+동사원형(몹시 ~하고 싶은)’의 형태로 쓰이므로 eager 뒤에 to subscribe가 적절하다. (C) 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(we already have)을 이끌어 선 행사 the OTT service를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므 로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.

Marketers use (B)psychological tactics to influence,

ⓒMake wiser choices, it’s essential to understand

Imagine you are in a shopping center, walking by

$500. Five hundred dollars for a pair of shoes? You

ⓔlooks similar for $200. After seeing the sneakers
for $500, you think the $200 sneakers are a good

rely too much on the first piece of information we

point,
to interpret
new
information. This can

“Start your free 14-day trial."
“Click here and start your free trial now.”
“Why wait? Start your trial today.”
These are typical phrases used in advertisements.
Imagine an OTT (Over the Top) media service
provider offers you a free premium service for a
month. The advertisement reassures you that you
can cancel the service anytime within the month.
Marketers do this because after we use a product,
we start to feel a sense of ownership, which makes
it difficult to give up the product or switch to a
different
one.
In
other
words,
we
tend
to
(A)______________ items that we already own more
than we would if they didn’t belong to us. Then,
how can we overcome this psychological ownership
bias? Above all, be aware of the “free trial” trap.
Once you fall into a trap, it’s important to
remember that it can be difficult to escape. Before
you sign up for a free trial, remind yourself about
how marketers use tactics that make you bond with
their products. Cancel the product or service if you
don’t need it.
How
do
you
feel
when
you
look
at
an
advertisement that says, “Only one left!” or “Today
only: 50% off”? If you don’t buy the product, it
feels like you are missing out on a great deal.
Whatever the product is, consumers are usually
influenced by a sense of urgency and scarcity.
People think a product or service is more valuable
or desirable when they believe the supply is limited.
It can be challenging to ignore the temptation of
urgency and scarcity while shopping. Still, whenever
you feel anxious about (B)______________ a great deal,
you should remember that there are plenty of
alternative items that are just as good or better.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(A)                   (B)
choices: overestimate        obtaining
downplay        passing up
overrate        losing out on
underestimate         overlooking
prize                securing
solution: (A) 앞 문장에서 우리가 제품을 사용한 후 주인의식을 느껴, 그 상품을 포기하거나 다른 것으로 바꾸는 것이 어려워진다고 했으므로 우리가 이미 소유한 상품을 소유하지 않은 것보다 ‘과대평가한다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 overestimate(과 대평가하다), overrate(과대평가하다), prize(높이 평가하다, 소 중히 여기다)가 적절하다. (B) 하나만 남았다거나 오늘만 할인한다는 광고를 볼 때 우리 는 그 제품을 사지 않으면 대단한 물건을 놓치고 있는 것 같 은 기분이 든다고 했고, 소비자들은 긴박감과 희소성에 영향을 받는다고 좋은 거래를 ‘놓치는 것’에 대해 불안해한다는 흐름 이 자연스럽다. 따라서 passing up(놓치는 것), losing out on (놓치는 것), overlooking(간과하는 것)이 적절하다.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

Few people say they enjoy waiting in a long line
to buy a ticket or product. In real life, however,
people often put up with waiting in line for hours
to purchase a popular product. When a particular
fashion item, a beauty product, or a brand becomes
popular, we may feel pushed to purchase the
product to keep up with the trend. In other words,
we often choose to do something because everyone
else is doing it. The more people do something,
the more likely we are to follow the act. How can
we prevent others from influencing our shopping
decisions? The next time you feel compelled to buy
a product in high demand because others do it,
first ask yourself if you really need it. Don’t be
afraid to stand out from the crowd.
choices: a strategy to resist the influence of social trendson buying behavior

hundred dollars for a pair of shoes? You doubt
your own eyes and walk into the store. In the
store, you find another pair of sneakers that looks

you think the $200 sneakers are a good bargain
and buy them even though you don’t need a new
pair of sneakers. In this way, we sometimes rely too
much on the first piece of information ⓑwe receive.
We use it as an anchor, or a reference point, to
interpret new information. This can lead to a hasty
judgment. How can we avoid having an anchoring
bias? We should think twice and compare prices.
The ⓒmore information we have about a product
and its price range, the less likely we are to fall
prey to an anchoring bias.
Few people say ⓓthat they enjoy waiting in a
long line to buy a ticket or product. In real life,
however, people often put up with waiting in line
for hours to purchase a popular product. When a
particular fashion item, a beauty product, or a
brand becomes popular, we may feel pushed to
purchase the product to keep up with the trend. In
other words, we often choose to do something
because everyone else is doing it. The more people
do something, the more likely we are to follow the
act. How can we prevent others from influencing
our shopping decisions? The next time you feel
compelled to buy a product in high demand
because others do it, first ask yourself ⓔif you
really need it. Don’t be afraid to stand out from
the crowd.

“Start your free 14-day trial."
“Click here and start your free trial now.”
“Why wait? Start your trial today.”
These are typical phrases used in advertisements.
Imagine an OTT (Over the Top) media service
provider offers you a free premium service for a
month. The advertisement reassures you that you
can cancel the service anytime within the month.
Marketers do this because after we use a product,
we start to feel a sense of ownership, which makes
it difficult to give up the product or switch to a
different one. In other words, we tend to overvalue
items that we already own more than we would if
they didn’t belong to us. Then, how can we
overcome this psychological ownership bias? Above
all, be aware of the “free trial” trap. Once you fall
into a trap, it’s important to remember that it can
be difficult to escape. Before you sign up for a free
trial, remind yourself about how marketers use
tactics that make you bond with their products.
Cancel the product or service if you don’t need it.

Being aware of marketing tactics that promoteemotional attachment to a product is essentialto avoid the free trial trap.
If a product or service is no longer needed, oneshould cease using it immediately.

Few people say they enjoy waiting in a long line
to buy a ticket or product. In real life, however,
people often put up with waiting in line for hours
to purchase a popular product. When a particular
fashion item, a beauty product, or a brand becomes
popular, we may feel pushed to purchase the
product to keep up with the trend. In other words,
we often choose to do something because everyone
else is doing it. The more people do something,
the more likely we are to follow the act. How can
we prevent others from influencing our shopping
decisions? The next time you feel compelled to buy
a product in high demand because others do it,
first ask yourself if you really need it. Don’t be
afraid to stand out from the crowd.

Waiting in a long line is sometimes required toobtain a highly desired product.
Seek items that showcase your distinct personalityinstead of following others.

To prevent unnecessary purchases, create a detailedshopping list.

village, Gando. Instead of using more conventional
modern materials like concrete, glass, and steel, he
chose to use clay, embracing the traditional building
methods of Africa. He made bricks by mixing clay,
a locally available material, with 10% cement. This
mixture helps keep classrooms ⓑcool during hot
weather. Additionally, he used bricks with holes in
them to make the ceiling and built a high roof
ⓒused a contemporary architectural system to let
hot air escape. The large overhanging roof provides

stones for the school foundation and women

Africa. It now includes temporary and permanent
structures in Denmark, Germany, Italy, Switzerland,
the UK, and the USA. Perhaps not too surprisingly,
his works outside of Africa are influenced by his
experiences in Gando. A perfect example is the
colorful Serpentine Pavilion in London. Since the
year 2000, the Serpentine Gallery in the UK has
annually invited distinguished architects from around
the world to design a pavilion, which provides a
place of rest for visitors. In 2017, the honor was
extended to Kéré. Drawing inspiration from his
hometown, where locals would gather to work,

cultural

circulation. The roof’s unique funnel design channels
rainwater toward

center.

Zaha Hadid (1950-2016) was a pioneering architect
known for her innovative designs. She was the first
woman to ever win the Pritzker Prize in 2004. It is
the Oscar Awards or the Nobel Prize of architecture.
Hadid’s architectural style was (A)characterized by
flowing,
curved
forms
and
a
departure
from
traditional geometry. She pushed the boundaries of
architecture and urban design with a distinctive
style (B)that places space at center stage.
Her notable works include the Vitra Fire Station in
Germany, the Sheikh Zayed Bridge, the Heydar
Aliyev Center, the Guangzhou Opera House in
China, and the London Aquatics Centre for the
2012 Olympics.
Vitra Fire Station
Built in a small German town on the borders of
Switzerland and France, the Vitra Fire Station was
Hadid’s first opportunity to bring her abstract
drawings and paintings to life in a physical form.
The dynamic feeling of motion was just beginning
to hint at the dawn of the future of Zaha Hadid’s
architecture, with her long journey to international
fame already starting.
Sheikh Zayed Bridge
The magnificent four-lane highway bridge reflects

What about Martin Luther King, Jr.? The original

in stone, and he had the freedom to improvise.

We often read stories about extremely intelligent,
gifted children. We might see an elementary school
student who can play the most difficult classical
music, a young boy who can do complicated math
in his head, or a little girl who can get into a
famous university before her 13th birthday. The

these
extremely

young

(B)[excellent / poor] social skills or low emotional

are too awkward, strange, and naive to succeed in
the normal world. However, this theory is almost
certainly wrong. Extremely gifted children usually
have normal social skills and most of them are
comfortable going to parties, talking with friends,
and dealing with bosses or customers.
Instead, what seems to hold them back is their
way of learning. All the time a gifted child spends
memorizing Mozart is time he can’t spend learning
how to compose music himself. All the time an
extremely intelligent child spends studying for
university tests is time she can’t spend learning how
to think independently. In summary, these children
tend to spend all of their time memorizing old
ideas and skills but very little time coming up with
new ideas or skills. This, unfortunately, is what most
education (C)[encourages / forbids] students to do.

(B)
(C)

body:
Francis Kéré, a winner of the Pritzker Prize, was
born in Burkina Faso, one of the poorest countries
in Africa. The region in Africa (A)[which / in which]
he grew up didn’t have any electricity or running
water. When he was seven, he had to move 13 km
away to attend school. He made history in his
village as its first student ever. The conditions of
the school (B)[which / where] he attended were
very poor. The classroom, hastily constructed from
cement, was filled with over a hundred children.
With temperatures often exceeding 40 degrees and
without any form of lighting, it was a challenging
environment for learning. Although Kéré could
(C)[give / have given] up his dreams, he remained
determined to study.
While still a young student, he was awarded a
scholarship to study carpentry in Germany. He
finished his high school studies in Germany and went
on to attend university there as well. Even though he
became a globally recognized architect in Germany,
he has not forgotten his roots. His architectural
designs are deeply influenced by his love for Africa
and a profound sense of pride in his people.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: in which   whichgive
in which   whichhave given
which   wheregive
in which   wherehave given
which   whichhave given
solution: (A) 완전한 절(he grew up)을 이끌어 선행사 The region in Africa를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 형태로 써 야 하며, 선행사 The region in Africa는 장소를 나타내므로 장소와 어 울리는 전치사 in과 관계대명사 which를 함께 쓴 in which가 적절하다. (B) 동사의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(he attended)을 이끌어 선행사 the school을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목 적격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. (C) 흐름상 ‘Kéré는 꿈을 포기할 수도 있었지만 (포기하기 않았다)’라는 의미로, 과거에 어떤 일이 일어날 가능성이 있었지만 실제로는 일어나 지 않았음을 나타내고 있으므로 could have p.p.의 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 조동사 could 뒤에는 have given이 이어지는 것이 적절하다.

Gando Primary School
For his first project, he managed to raise ＄30,000
to build an elementary school in his native village,
Gando. Instead of using more ⓐconventional modern
materials like concrete, glass, and steel, he chose to
use clay, embracing the traditional building methods
of Africa. He made bricks by mixing clay, a locally
available material, with 10% cement. This mixture
helps keep classrooms cool during hot weather.
Additionally, he used bricks with holes in them to
make the ceiling and built a high roof using a
ⓑcontemporary architectural system to let hot air
escape. The large ⓒoverhanging roof provides shade
and protects the clay bricks from heavy rain.

Lycée Schorge Secondary School is comprised of
nine ⓓdistinct modules. These modules house a
collection of classrooms and offices, all centered
around a main public courtyard. This design ensures
privacy
from
the
main
public
area
while
simultaneously
sheltering
and
protecting
the
courtyard against wind and dust.
Kéré ⓔtackled the problem of limited resources

the
building
using
bricks
made

body:
Gando Primary School
For his first project, he managed ⓐraising ＄30,000
to build an elementary school in his native village,
Gando. Instead of using more (A)______________
modern materials like concrete, glass, and steel, he
chose to use clay, embracing the traditional building
methods of Africa. He made bricks by mixing clay,
a locally available material, with 10% cement. This
mixture helps keep classrooms cool during hot
weather. Additionally, he used bricks with holes in
ⓑit to make the ceiling and built a high roof using
a contemporary architectural system to let hot air
escape. The large overhanging roof provides shade
and protects the clay bricks from heavy rain.
Lycée Schorge Secondary School
Located in Burkina Faso’s third largest city, the
Lycée Schorge Secondary School is comprised of
nine distinct modules. These modules house a
collection of classrooms and offices, all ⓒare
centered around a main public courtyard. This
design ensures privacy from the main public area
while simultaneously sheltering and protecting the
courtyard against wind and dust.
Kéré tackled the problem of limited resources
during the building’s construction by using materials
that were easy to find in the region in the same
manner as before. First of all, he built the walls of
the
building
using
bricks
made
from
readily
available stone in the region. These bricks help
(B)______________ the building by absorbing intense
daytime heat and later releasing it during the night.
As with many other buildings, an overhanging roof
protects the brick walls from the harsh African sun
while also facilitating air circulation below. ⓓCapture
fresh air and let hot air escape, Kéré also added
wind towers on top of each classroom. The school
is surrounded by a screen made from fast-growing
local eucalyptus trees. This screen provides more
than just protection against dust and wind. It also
creates casual spaces ⓔwhich students can gather
as they wait for their classes to begin.

choices: ⓐ: raising → to raise
ⓑ: it → them
ⓒ: are centered → centered
ⓓ: Capture → To capture
ⓔ: which → that
solution: ⓔ which → where 또는 in which (완전한 절(students ~ to begin)을 이끌어 장소를 나타내는 선행사 spaces를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 which를 that이 아니라 관계부사 where 또는 ‘전치사+관계대명사’ in which로 고친다.)

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

Francis Kéré, a winner of the Pritzker Prize, was
born in Burkina Faso, one of the poorest countries
in Africa. The region in Africa where he grew up
didn’t have any electricity or running water. When
he was seven, he had to move 13 km away to
attend school. He made history in his village as its
first student ever. The conditions of the school he
attended were very poor. The classroom, hastily
constructed from cement, was filled with over a
hundred
children.
With
temperatures
often
exceeding 40 degrees and without any form of
lighting, it was a challenging environment for
learning. Although Kéré could have given up his
dreams, he remained determined to study.
While still a young student, he was awarded a
scholarship to study carpentry in Germany. He
finished his high school studies in Germany and
went on to attend university there as well. Even
though he became a globally recognized architect
in Germany, _______________________________________. His
architectural designs are deeply influenced by his
love for Africa and a profound sense of pride in his
people.
choices: he ignored the link between his success and hispast
he continued to cherish his cultural identity androots
he was more interested in other regions than inGermany
he wanted to work only within the African continent
he only sought to modernize Africa with Westerntechnology지학사(신상근) 3과
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

Sister Carla wanted to help the Hansen’s patients
in as many ways as she could. She raised pigs with
the patients to help them become economically
independent. She started to learn Korean so she
could understand each individual’s problems more
deeply. She struggled with the language at first, but
after
about
two
years,
she
was
able
to
communicate with local people freely and truly
understand
the
patients’
specific
challenges.
Additionally, she went to a hospital in Spain to
study Hansen’s disease and earn a nurse’s assistant
certification.
When she first began treating Hansen’s patients,
she was able to treat them with only the small
amount of medicine she received from German aid
agencies. “The saddest thing at the time was not
the fact that there was a lack of medicine, but the
prejudice towards the Hansen’s patients. Because of
that, the children of Hansen’s patients were not
accepted by normal schools,” Sister Carla said. So
she _________________________________________. Otherwise,
more than a hundred children wouldn’t have
received proper education.
choices: encouraged the patients to move to anothervillage with schools
complained to the German aid agencies aboutthe lack of medicine
decided to stop providing medical support tofocus on education
founded a school for the children of Hansen’spatients in the village
focused on providing job training to the patients’children

body:
We meet many people and build many friendships.
We sometimes meet remarkable individuals who
sacrifice (A)[them / themselves] for those in need.
It’s their daily routine to help others, and they even
put others before themselves. Sister Carla is an
excellent example of such a person. Often (B)[calling
/ called] the angel with blue eyes, she devoted her
life to caring for patients with Hansen’s disease in
the remote village of Hoam, Gochang, Jeollabuk-do.
ⓐ1943년 이탈리아 Bernezzo에서 태어난 칼라 수녀
는 19살에 수녀가 되어 결국 120명이 넘는 전쟁고아
들을 돌보게 되었다. I thought that instead of
starting a family and caring for my own children
only, I could devote my life to caring for more
children.” She added, “I also became a nun because
I wanted to fulfill the dream of my late brother,
(C)[who / that] wanted to become a priest but
passed away before he could.”
The 25-year-old Sister Carla came to Korea in
1968 after hearing about many war orphans and
Hansen’s patients in Korea. Back then, people
excluded Hansen’s patients from the general public
due to various prejudices. People falsely believed that
Hansen’s disease was highly contagious, and also
felt uncomfortable with the appearance of Hansen’s
patients. Nowhere was the place for those patients,
and their miserable lives were passed on to their
own children. For Sister Carla, however, Hansen’s
patients were equally noble human beings. She
accepted the pain of those patients as her own.

(B) 뒤의 완전한 절(she ~ Jeollabuk-do)과 접속사 없이 콤마(,) 로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주 어인 she가 파란 눈을 가진 천사라고 ‘불리는’ 대상이므로 수 동의 의미인 과거분사 called가 적절하다. people,
it
changes
your

became a nun at the age of 19 and ended up
caring for more than 120 war orphans. “I thought
that instead of starting a family and caring for my
own children only, I could devote my life to caring
for more children.”
(A) Back then, people excluded Hansen’s patients from
the general public due to various prejudices.
People falsely believed that Hansen’s disease was
highly contagious, and also felt uncomfortable
with the appearance of Hansen’s patients.
(B) Nowhere was the place for those patients, and
their miserable lives were passed on to their
own children. For Sister Carla, however, Hansen’s
patients were equally noble human beings.
(C) She added, “I also became a nun because I
wanted to fulfill the dream of my late brother,
who wanted to become a priest but passed away
before he could.” The 25-year-old Sister Carla
came to Korea in 1968 after hearing about many
war orphans and Hansen’s patients in Korea.
She accepted the pain of those patients as her
own.

(B) 뒤에서 사람들은 한센병이 전염성이 매우 높다고 잘못 믿 었다고 했으므로 여러 가지 편견으로 인해 한센병 환자들을 일반 대중으로부터 고립시켰다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 isolated(고립시켰다)가 적절하다. (C) 앞에서 사람들은 편견 때문에 한센병 환자들을 멀리했고, 그들을 위한 곳은 어디에도 없었고 그들의 자녀들마저 비참한 삶을 대물림되었다고 했으며, 역접 연결사 however(그러나)로 이어지므로 ‘그 환자들도 똑같이 고귀한 인간이다‘라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 dignified(고귀한)가 적절하다.

축구가 더욱 발전할 수 있다 는 주어진 문장 뒤에는, 이러한 변화를 this change(이 러한 변화)로 받아 However(그러나)를 사용해 기술 발 전에 따른 반대와 우려가 있음을 언급한 (C), 이어서 (C)의 마지막 문장에서 VAR에 대한 반대를 한 가지 사 례로 제시한 후, Also(또한)를 사용해 반대와 우려에 해 당하는 또 다른 사례로 웨어러블 기기와 안면 인식 데 이터로 인한 사생활 침해 문제를 언급한 (A), 마지막으 로 Nonetheless(그럼에도 불구하고)를 사용해 이러한 단점들이 존재함에도 불구하고, 스포츠 기술의 장점과 단점을 균형 있게 관리한다면 앞으로의 축구는 선수, 팀, 그리고 팬들에게 더욱 흥미로운 스포츠가 될 것이 라고 정리한 (B)로 마무리되는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 15) ⓐ With technology shifting so quickly ⓑ which causes concerns about fairness ⓒ arguing that it disrupts the natural flow of games : ⓐ 전치사 With의 목적어로 절이 이어질 수 없으므로, ‘with+명사(구)+분사(~하면서, ~한 채로)‘의 구조를 갖는 ’with 분사구문‘이 되어야 한다. 따라서 technology를 수 식하는 분사 자리이며 technology를 ‘변화하는‘ 주체로 보아 동사 shifts를 능동의 의미인 현재분사 shifting으로 고친다. ⓑ 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which의 선행사가 앞 절 전체로 단수이므로 cause를 단수동사 causes로 고친다. ⓒ 완전한 절(Many ~ system)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주 어 Many(많은 사람들)가 ’주장하는‘ 주체이자 뒤에 목적 어(that ~ games)가 이어지므로 argue를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 arguing으로 고친다. 16) ④: 스포츠 기술의 장단점을 균형 있게 관리하면 향후 몇 년은 흥미진진한 시간이 될 것이라고 했으므로 ④ ‘스 포츠 기술은 축구에 부정적인 영향을 미치지만, 우리는 그것을 즐기는 것 외에는 할 수 있는 일이 없다.’는 일 치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 축구는 기술 발전으로부터 혜택을 받을 수 있는 스 포츠이다. ② 웨어러블 기기와 안면 인식 데이터는 개인정보 보 호 문제와 관련이 있다. ③ 축구 구단의 재정적 자원은 구단이 기술로부터 얼 마나 많은 혜택을 받는지에 영향을 미칠 수 있다. ⑤ 비디오 판독(VAR) 시스템과 같은 스포츠 기술들은 많은 사람들의 반대에 직면해 있다. 17) ③: 축구에서는 심판 판정에 대한 이견이 많이 발생하지만 VAR과 같은 기술은 심판이 정확한 판정을 내리는 것을 도와 공정한 경기를 보장하는데, 2022년 월드컵 당시 사우디아라비아와 아르헨티나의 경기에서 아르헨티나 의 세 골이 VAR 시스템에 의해 오프사이드 반칙으로 취소된 사례를 언급하고 있으므로, 정확한 판정과 공정 한 경기를 보장하는 기술의 도입으로 심판 판정에 대 한 이견이 없었다는 흐름이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 이 기술 도입 이후에 생긴 일로, 빈칸에는 ③ ‘선수들은 심 판 판정에 대해 중대한 항의를 하는 것을 거의 완전히 중단했다’가 가장 알맞다. 오답 ① 경기의 흐름은 과거에 그랬던 것보다 훨씬 더 원활 해졌다 ② 강팀과 약팀 사이의 실력 격차는 시간이 지나면서 크게 줄어들었다 ④ 선수들의 경기 운영은 이전보다 경기 중에 훨씬 더 공격적으로 변했다 ⑤ 선수들이 심판 판정에 불만을 표출하는 사례가 더 많이 있었다 18) ②: (A) 골라인 기술은 각 골대에 설치된 7대의 카메라로 영상을 촬영하여 공이 골라인을 넘었는지를 판단하고 심판에게 알리는 기술이라고 했으므로, 공의 정확한 위 치를 계산한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 calculate (계산하다)가 적절하다. predict 예측하다 (B) 앞에서 헤딩한 선수가 득점자로 기록되었다고 했 고, However(그러나)로 연결되어 ‘그러나 정정되었다’라 고 했으므로 왼쪽에서 공을 찼던 선수의 골로 인정되 었다는 상반된 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 crediting(~ 의 공으로 믿는[인정되는] 것)이 적절하다. deny 부인하다 (C) 앞에서 공이 차였을 때 그래프에서 움직임이 감지 되었지만, 헤딩이 시도되었을 때 그래프는 그대로 있었 다고 했으므로, 인과관계를 나타내는 연결어 As a result(결과적으로) 뒤에 공을 찬 선수가 득점자임이 기 술적으로 증명되었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 proven(증명된)이 적절하다. disprove 틀렸음을 입증하다 19) ②: 아스널, 첼시, 리버풀, 맨체스터 시티, 맨체스터 유나이 티드, 그리고 토트넘이 ‘빅 6’로 여겨지는데, 왜 이 팀 들이 ‘빅 6’인지 이유가 언급되지 않았으므로 ② ‘특정 팀들이 ’빅 6‘라고 불리는 이유는 무엇인가?’는 답할 수 없는 질문이다. 오답 ① 세 축구팀들 중 어느 팀이 가장 짧은 역사를 가지 고 있는가? (→잉글리시 프리미어 리그이다.) ③ 바르셀로나와 레알 마드리드의 경기가 “엘 클라시 코”라고 불리는 이유는 무엇인가? (→두 팀은 너무나 강력한 라이벌이어서 그들의 경기는 ‘고전’을 의미하는 “엘 클라시코”라고 불린다.) ④ 게겐프레싱을 사용하는 팀은 공을 잃은 후 어떻게 반응하는가? (→뒤로 물러나지 않고 즉시 공격적으로 압박한다) ⑤ 잉글리시 프리미어리그, 라리가, 분데스리가의 공통 점은 무엇인가? (→각 팀이 다른 모든 팀과 두 번씩 경 기하는 방식을 가진다.) 20) ④: (A) 주어 the league가 일곱 자매로 ‘정의되어‘ 온 대상 이므로 단수명사구인 주어에 수일치한 현재완료 수동태 (have/has been+p.p.) has been defined가 적절하다 (B) 등위접속사 and 뒤에 전치사구(with ~ defense)가 이중 쉼표로 삽입된 형태로, 주어 These teams에 이어 지는 동사 are와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되므로, 동사 made가 적절하다. 참고로 지금도 인기가 있기에 현재동사 are이 쓰였으며, 속담이 유명해진 것은 과거 일로 동사 made가 쓰였다. (C) 전치사 for의 목적어 자리이며 뒤에 명사 the best players가 이어지므로 동명사의 능동태 attracting이 적 절하다.

body:
Her love for the Hansen’s patients is also reflected
in her Korean name, “Kang Kalla.” She adopted the
Korean family name “Kang” when the first patient
she met at the Hoam Village told her, “I would really
like you to use my family name.” As her personal
name, she decided to use “Kalla,” which is the
Korean pronunciation of her Catholic name, “Carla.”
Sister Carla did her best to be there for anyone
who needed her help, but sadly she didn’t have
enough time to care for herself. She developed
rheumatism but didn’t treat the disease properly
because she was busy working for her patients.
(A)_____________, her toes became severely twisted.
Her twisted toes reminded her neighbors of ginger
roots, and so they called her toes “ginger feet.” She
devoted everything she had to the sick, lonely, and
poor while she lived very frugally. She wore a
30-year-old watch on her wrist and kept two
pencils shorter than her little finger on her desk.
(B)_____________, Sister Carla lived in the same tiny
home for over 50 years.

When she (A)[asked / was asked] how to live a
valuable life, she replied: “When you live only for
the benefit of yourself, your joy and happiness
become that much smaller. But when you open
your heart to other people, it changes your life.”
Sister Carla’s extraordinary life reminds us that we
all can make a difference and (B)[what / that]
through our actions we can bring about a positive
change in the lives of those who need help most.
As she said, being respectful, caring, and supportive
towards others can improve our society and also
(C)[bring / bringing] us happiness.

solution: (A) 부사절 접속사 When, 주어 she에 이어지는 동사 자리이며, she가 가치 있는 삶을 사는 방법에 대해 ‘질문 받은’ 대상이므 로 수동태(be+p.p.) was asked가 적절하다. (B) 동사 reminds, 간접목적어 us에 이어지는 첫 번째 직접목 적어로 쓰인 명사절(that we ~ difference)과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬 연결된 두 번째 직접목적어로, 완전한 절(through ~ help most)을 이끌어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다. (C) 조동사 can에 이어지는 동사원형 improve와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로 동사원형 bring이 적절하다.

body:
Born in Bernezzo, Italy in 1943, Sister Carla
became a nun at the age of 19 and ended up
caring for more than 120 war orphans. “I thought
that instead of starting a family and caring for my
own children only, I could devote my life to caring
for more children.” She added, “I also became a
nun because I wanted to fulfill the dream of my
late brother, who wanted to become a priest but
passed away before he could.”
The 25-year-old Sister Carla came to Korea in 1968
after hearing about many war orphans and Hansen’s
patients in Korea. Back then, people excluded
Hansen’s patients from the general public due to
various
prejudices.
People
falsely believed
that
Hansen’s disease was highly contagious, and also
felt uncomfortable with the appearance of Hansen’s
patients. Nowhere was the place for those patients,
and their miserable lives were passed on to their
own children. For Sister Carla, however, Hansen’s
patients were equally noble human beings. She
accepted the pain of those patients as her own.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: a nun’s life as a way to fulfill her brother’sunrealized dream
Sister Carla’s effort to overcome personal biastoward Hansen’s patients
Sister Carla’s choice to come to Korea in searchof a treatment for Hansen’s disease
the social isolation and hardship of Hansen’spatients in Korea during the 1960s
reasons Sister Carla became a nun and herselfless care for Hansen’s patients

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

<보기>
ⓐ reflect: to make someone remember something
that they must do
ⓑ adopt: to take someone else’s child into your
home and legally become its parent
ⓒ develop: to start to have a disease or illness

We meet many people and build many friendships.
We sometimes meet remarkable individuals who
sacrifice themselves for those in need. It’s their daily
routine to help others, and they even put others
(A)[before / after] themselves. Sister Carla is an
excellent example of such a person. Often called
the angel with blue eyes, she devoted her life to
caring for patients with Hansen’s disease in the
remote village of Hoam, Gochang, Jeollabuk-do.
Born in Bernezzo, Italy in 1943, Sister Carla
became a nun at the age of 19 and ended up
caring for more than 120 war orphans. “I thought
that instead of starting a family and caring for my
own children only, I could devote my life to caring
for more children.” She added, “I also became a
nun because I wanted to fulfill the dream of my
late brother, who wanted to become a priest but
passed away before he could.”
The 25-year-old Sister Carla came to Korea in
1968 after hearing about many war orphans and
Hansen’s patients in Korea. Back then, people
excluded Hansen’s patients from the general public
due to various prejudices. People falsely believed
that Hansen’s disease was highly contagious, and
also felt (B)[comfortable / uncomfortable] with the
appearance of Hansen’s patients. Nowhere was the
place for those patients, and their miserable lives
were passed on to their own children. For Sister
Carla, however, Hansen’s patients were equally
noble human beings. She accepted the (C)[pain /
relief] of those patients as her own.

(C)

(B) 앞에서 그 당시 여러 가지 편견 때문에 한센병 환자들을 일반 대중으로부터 배제되었는데, 한센병이 전염성이 매우 강 하다고 잘못 믿고 있었던 것에 이어, 배제될 만한 상황이 이어 져야 하므로 그들의 겉모습을 불편하게 여겼다는 흐름이 자연 스럽다. 따라서 uncomfortable(불편한)이 적절하다. (C) 한센병 환자들은 사회에서 배제되고, 오해와 편견 속에서 비참한 삶을 살았으며, 그것이 그들의 자식들에게도 대물림되 었으나, 칼라 수녀는 한센병 환자들이 똑같이 고귀하고 여겼기 에 그들의 고통을 자신의 고통으로 받아들였다는 흐름이 자연 스럽다. 따라서 pain(고통)이 적절하다. 지학사(신상근) 4과 정답 본 콘텐츠는 해당 출판사로부터 교과서 라이센스를 획득하여 이그잼포유에서 제작하였습니다. 본 콘텐츠에 대한 저작권은 이그잼포유가 소유하고 있으며, 콘텐츠의 전부 또는 일부를 무단 전재하거나 배포하는 것은 저작권법에 의한 법적 책임 을 물을 수 있습니다. 본 콘텐츠의 레이아웃 및 편집에 대한 저작권 침해 행위 또한 금지하고 있습니다. 영어I 지학사(신상근) 4과 예상문제 4회 - 객관식(선다형) 1. ① 2. 주관식 3. ② 4. 주관식 5. ③ 6. ⑤ 7. ③ 8. ③ 9. ⑤ 10. 주관식 11. 주관식 12. ⑤

Traditionally, members of a whole village ⓐ[work /
works] together to build and repair homes in rural
Burkina Faso. In keeping with this cultural practice,
Kéré encouraged the villagers of Gando ⓑ[taking / to
take] part in the construction process. His objective
was for them to make the place on their own.
Children gathered stones for the school foundation
and women brought water for brick manufacturing. He
also trained the young members of the village and
then they collaborated on the construction. These
trained workers have since used these new skills to
build schools and houses in other communities.
Furthermore, he made all the architectural plans for
the school construction available to anyone in the
village, which made ⓒ[it / them] easier for two
nearby villages to build their own schools. Thanks to
the success of this project, the number of students
increased from 120 to a remarkable 700.

Francis Kéré, a winner of the Pritzker Prize, was
born in Burkina Faso, one of the poorest countries
in Africa. The region in Africa where he grew up
didn’t have any electricity or running water. When
he was seven, he had to move 13 km away to
attend school. He made history in his village as its
first student ever. The conditions of the school he
attended were very poor. The classroom, hastily
constructed from cement, was filled with over a
hundred children. With temperatures often exceeding
40 degrees and without any form of lighting, it was
a challenging environment for learning. Although
Kéré could have given up his dreams, he remained
determined to study.
While still a young student, he was awarded a
scholarship to study carpentry in Germany. He
finished his high school studies in Germany and
went on to attend university there as well. Even
though he became a globally recognized architect
in Germany, he has not forgotten his roots. His
architectural designs are deeply influenced by his
love for Africa and a profound sense of pride in his
people.

and eventually became a world-renowned architect,

his cultural roots through his architecture.
(A)
(B)

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

Located in Burkina Faso’s third largest city, the Lycée
Schorge Secondary School is comprised of nine
distinct modules. These modules house a collection of
classrooms and offices, all centered around a main
public courtyard. This design ensures privacy from the
main public area while simultaneously sheltering and
protecting the courtyard against wind and dust.
Kéré tackled the problem of limited resources
during the building’s construction by using materials
that were easy to find in the region in the same
manner as before. First of all, he built the walls of
the
building
using
bricks
made
from
readily
available stone in the region. These bricks help cool
the building by absorbing intense daytime heat and
later releasing it during the night.
As with many other buildings, an overhanging roof
protects the brick walls from the harsh African sun
while also facilitating air circulation below. To
capture fresh air and let hot air escape, Kéré also
added wind towers on top of each classroom. The
school is surrounded by a screen made from
fast-growing local eucalyptus trees. This screen
provides more than just protection against dust and
wind. It also creates casual spaces where students
can gather as they wait for their classes to begin.

Zaha Hadid (1950-2016) was a pioneering architect
known for her innovative designs. She was the first
woman to ever win the Pritzker Prize in 2004. It is
the Oscar Awards or the Nobel Prize of architecture.
Hadid’s architectural style was characterized by
flowing,
curved
forms
and
a
departure
from
traditional geometry. She pushed the boundaries of
architecture and urban design with a distinctive
style that places space at center stage.
Her notable works include the Vitra Fire Station in
Germany, the Sheikh Zayed Bridge, the Heydar Aliyev
Center, the Guangzhou Opera House in China, and
the London Aquatics Centre for the 2012 Olympics.
Vitra Fire Station
Built in a small German town on the borders of
Switzerland and France, the Vitra Fire Station was
Hadid’s first opportunity to bring her abstract
drawings and paintings to life in a physical form.
The dynamic feeling of motion was just beginning
to hint at the dawn of the future of Zaha Hadid’s
architecture, with her long journey to international
fame already starting.
Sheikh Zayed Bridge
The magnificent four-lane highway bridge reflects
how Hadid’s curving forms translate to functional
architecture. The curved bridge, which forms a joint
between Abu Dhabi island and the southern Gulf
shore, was inspired by sand hills, once again
showing how Hadid’s architecture holds a distorted
mirror up to nature. Stretching a half of a mile
(842 meters), it is said to be one of the most
sophisticated bridges ever constructed.

body:
If you want to have good ideas, you must have
numerous ideas. Traditionally, people follow the
saying that they prefer “quality over quantity.”
However, in the case of ideas, quantity and quality
are equally important. Highly creative individuals do
not actually produce better ideas than average
ones. Instead, they produce more ideas. Their
increased idea output means that they are more
likely to hit on something brilliant.
An excellent example is Pablo Picasso. Picasso is
famous for a handful of artworks. However, few
people realize that Picasso’s portfolio includes 2,800
ceramics, 1,800 paintings, 1,200 sculptures, and
more than 12,000 drawings. (A) Again, only a
fraction of them became famous. (B) Likewise,
Mozart composed over 600 pieces before his death
at age 35, only a handful of which are recognized
as particularly creative. (C) Einstein also had more
than 248 publications, but many of them didn’t
have much impact. (D) This way, you have more of
a chance that one or two will be outstanding. (E)
Just pour out whatever comes to mind and
separate the gems from the rocks.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Traditional belief favors the quality of ideas overthe number of ideas.
Creative individuals differ from others mainly inthe quantity of output.
Picasso’s great success came from concentratingon only a few select pieces.
Mozart and Einstein show that a large body ofwork raises the chance of brilliance.
People should produce ideas freely and thenpick the most valuable ones for success.
solution: Picasso의 포트폴리오에 도자기 2,800점, 회화 1,800점, 조각 1,200점, 그리고 1만 2,000점이 넘는 드로잉이 포함되어 있고 그것들 중 일부만이 유명해졌다고 했으므로 ❸ ‘Pablo Picasso 의 큰 성공은 오직 몇몇 선택된 작품들에만 집중한 것에서 비 롯되었다.‘는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

We often read stories about extremely intelligent,
gifted children. We might see an elementary school
student who can play the most difficult classical
music, a young boy who can do complicated math
in his head, or a little girl who can get into a
famous university before her 13th birthday. The
surprising thing, though, is that these children aren’t
usually very successful as adults.
Some people might explain this by assuming that
these extremely gifted young people have poor
social skills or low emotional intelligence. In other
words, these gifted children are too awkward,
strange, and naive to succeed in the normal world.
However, this theory is almost certainly wrong.
Extremely gifted children usually have normal social
skills and most of them are comfortable going to
parties, talking with friends, and dealing with bosses
or customers.

the underlying factors that cause highly giftedchildren to lack social skills

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

Generate a Lot of Ideas
If you want to have good ideas, you must have
numerous ideas. Traditionally, people follow the
saying that they prefer “quality over quantity.”
(A) Instead, they produce more ideas. Their increased
idea output means that they are more likely to
hit on something brilliant.
(B) However, in the case of ideas, quantity and
quality are equally important. Highly creative
individuals do not actually produce better ideas
than average ones.
(C) An excellent example is Pablo Picasso. Picasso is
famous for a handful of artworks. However, few
people realize that Picasso’s portfolio includes
2,800 ceramics, 1,800 paintings, 1,200 sculptures,
and more than 12,000 drawings.
Again, only a fraction of them became famous.
Likewise, Mozart composed over 600 pieces before
his death at age 35, only a handful of which are
recognized as particularly creative. Einstein also had
more than 248 publications, but many of them
didn’t have much impact. The lesson here is to
produce a large volume of work. This way, you
have more of a chance that one or two will be
outstanding. Just pour out whatever comes to mind
and separate the gems from the rocks.

We are frequently told that procrastination is our
worst enemy. Almost every self-help book describes
successful people as being those who can overcome
procrastination. However, several moments of genius
have stemmed from procrastination. Great originals
know how to utilize procrastination as a strategy in
their idea production. Procrastination encourages
gradual progress rather than rapid progress, which
leaves your brain open to a wider range of ideas.
While
procrastination
may
be
the
enemy
of
productivity, it can be a resource for creativity.
Few people know that Leondardo da Vinci was a
chronic procrastinator. It took him 16 years to
complete the Mona Lisa. Some of the things that
took his attention away from work, like learning
optics, transformed the way he modeled light and
made him into a much better painter.
What about Martin Luther King, Jr.? The original
script of his speech, believe it or not, didn’t contain
the words “I have a dream.” The night before the
biggest speech of his life, he was up past 3 a.m.
rewriting his script. He was sitting in the audience
waiting for his turn to go onto the stage and still
writing notes on his script. After he got on stage,
11 minutes in, he heard Mahalia Jackson, his favorite
singer, cry out: “Tell them about the dream, Martin.”
Encouraged by a shout from the audience, he drew
upon some of his past talks, and the result became
the landmark speech “I have a dream.” By delaying
the task of finalizing the speech until the very last
minute, he left himself open to the widest range of
possible ideas. The text wasn’t set in stone, and he
had the freedom to improvise.
choices: Procrastination is often viewed as a detrimentalhabit that successful people must overcome.
Delay is sometimes useful as it helps the mindremain receptive to diverse ideas.
Da Vinci’s work was enhanced by his tendencyto explore other fields like optics.
Martin Luther King, Jr.’s speech was powerfulbecause he was prepared with a final script inadvance.
Putting off completing a task helps peopleremain free to improvise.

(C) 주어와 동사 사이에 이중콤마로 연결사 however가 삽입된 형태로, 주어 The above stories에 상응하는 복 수 동사 show가 적절하다. 16) ⑤: ⓔ memorize(암기하다) → improvise(즉흥적으로 하다) 17) ②: 똑똑하고 재능 있는 아이들이 대개 성인이 되었을 때 그다지 성공적이지 않다는 점을 언급하며, 일부 사람들 은 그 이유가 이 아이들의 사교성 부족이나 낮은 정서 적 지능에서 비롯된다고 가정하지만, 글의 마지막에서 이러한 이론이 틀렸다고 분명히 밝히고 있으므로, 이 글의 바로 뒤에 이어질 내용으로 적절한 것은 ② ‘매우 재능 있는 아이들이 성인의 성공을 거두는 데 실패하 는 실제 이유들’이다. 오답 ① 영재 아이들에 의해 보여지는 비범한 재능들의 다 양한 사례들 ③ 매우 재능 있는 아이들을 사회적 기술이 부족하게 만드는 근본적인 요인들 ④ 낮은 감성 지능이 영재 아이들의 미래 성공에 미치 는 영향 ⑤ 매우 재능 있는 어린 개인들의 사회적 기술을 향상 시키기 위한 실질적인 방법들 18) ②: 통상적으로 사람들이 ‘양보다 질’을 선호한다는 말을 따 른다는 주어진 글 뒤에, However(그러나)로 시작하여 아이디어의 경우에는 양과 질이 똑같이 중요하다고 하 며 앞의 통념을 반박하는 (B), (B)의 마지막 문장에서 창의적인 사람들이 평균적인 사람들보다 더 나은 아이 디어를 내는 것은 아니라는 점을 밝힌 뒤, Instead(그 대신에)로 시작하여 창의적인 사람들을 they로 받아 그 들이 더 좋은 아이디어를 만드는 것이 아니라 더 많은 아이디어를 만들어 낸다는 대조적인 내용을 제시하는 (A), 마지막으로 ‘An excellent example is Pablo Picasso.’로 시작하여, 앞서 제시된 주장을 구체적인 사 례를 통해 설명하며 (C)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 19) ③: ⓒ same(똑같은) → opposite(정반대의) 20) ④: 요약문 독창적인 사고는 현장 유지를 (A)거스르고 능동 적으로 더 나은 대안을 (B)찾는 것을 포함하는데, 이는 높은 가격에 의문을 제기하고 (C)혁신적인 비즈니스 모 델을 만든 한 온라인 안경 회사가 예시로 보여진다. 오답 ① 수용하는 것 피하는 것 독창적인 ② 복종하는 것 추구하는 것 관습적인 ③ 도전하는 것 탐색하는 것 예측 가능한 ⑤ 논쟁하는 것 무시하는 것 참신한 21) you are either born with it, or you aren’t : • ‘A거나 혹은 B'의 의미를 갖는 상관접속사 either은 either A, or B를 이용하므로, ’그것을 가지고 태어나거나 혹은 그렇지 않다’를 영작해야 하기 위해, 주어 you, 동사 are 뒤에 either를 쓰고, 보어 born과 전치사구 with it을 이어 쓴다. • or과 주어 you 뒤에 ‘그것을 가지고 태어나지 않는다’를 뜻하는 aren't born with it에서 앞 절의 반복되는 born with it이 생략된 대동사 aren’t를 이어 쓴다. 22) ④: Martin Luther King, Jr.는 연설 직전까지 원고를 수정했 으며, 무대 위에서도 즉흥적으로 내용을 변경했다고 했 으므로 ④ ‘Martin Luther King, Jr.의 연설은 그가 사전 에 최종 원고로 준비되었기 때문에 강렬했다.‘는 일치하 지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 미루는 습관은 종종 성공적인 사람들이 극복해야만 하는 해로운 습관으로 여겨진다. detrimental 유해한, 해로운 ② 지연은 때때로 마음이 다양한 아이디어들에 대해 수 용적인 상태를 유지하도록 도와주기 때문에 유용하다. ③ 다빈치의 작품은 광학과 같은 다른 분야를 탐구하는 그의 경향에 의해 향상되었다. ⑤ 과업을 완료하는 것을 미루는 것은 사람들이 즉흥적 으로 행동할 자유를 유지하도록 돕는다.

there was a lack of medicine, but the prejudice
towards the Hansen’s patients. Because of that, the
children of Hansen’s patients were not accepted by
normal schools,” Sister Carla said. (B)_____________ she
founded a school for the children of Hansen’s patients
in the village. Otherwise, more than a hundred
children wouldn’t have received proper education.

Her love for the Hansen’s patients is also reflected

who needed her help, but sadly she didn’t have
enough time to care for herself. She developed

roots, and so they called her toes “ginger feet.”

lonely, and poor while she lived very frugally.
She wore a 30-year-old watch on her wrist and
kept two pencils shorter than her little finger on
her desk. Additionally, Sister Carla lived in the same
tiny home for over 50 years.

body:
Born in Bernezzo, Italy in 1943, Sister Carla
became a nun at the age of 19 and ended up
caring for more than 120 war orphans. “I thought
that instead of starting a family and caring for my
own children only, I could devote my life to caring
for more children.” She added, “I also became a
nun because I wanted to fulfill the dream of my
late brother, who wanted to become a priest but
passed away before he could.”
The 25-year-old Sister Carla came to Korea in
1968 after hearing about many war orphans and
Hansen’s patients in Korea. Back then, people
excluded Hansen’s patients from the general public
due to various prejudices. People falsely believed
that Hansen’s disease was highly contagious, and
also felt uncomfortable with the appearance of
Hansen’s patients. Nowhere was the place for those
patients, and their miserable lives were passed on
to their own children. For Sister Carla, however,
Hansen’s patients were equally noble human beings.
She accepted the pain of those patients as her own.

dangerous for players in the long run. This is why
the Football Association prohibits players under the
age of 12 from performing headers altogether. It
also
recommends
that
all
players,
including
professionals, shouldn’t be exposed to more than
10 headers a week in training. So, soccer teams

players can practice headers without the risk of
brain damage. Artificial intelligence is also being
used to analyze players’ medical profiles, fitness
assessment results, and performance data to identify
those who might be at risk of suffering an injury.

enjoyable. Fans can now easily purchase tickets

tickets. Furthermore, in addition to live broadcasting
on television, fans can enjoy the game at home or

(C) 앞부분에서는 스포츠 기술에 대한 반대 의견과 우려가 제 시되고 마지막 문장이 Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고)로 이 어지므로 앞의 부정적인 내용과 대조되는 내용이 이어져야 한 다. 따라서 장단점을 균형 있게 고려한다면 미래는 긍정적일 것이라는 흐름이 자연스러우므로 exciting(흥미진진한)이 적절 하다. 지학사(신상근) 2과 정답 본 콘텐츠는 해당 출판사로부터 교과서 라이센스를 획득하여 이그잼포유에서 제작하였습니다. 본 콘텐츠에 대한 저작권은 이그잼포유가 소유하고 있으며, 콘텐츠의 전부 또는 일부를 무단 전재하거나 배포하는 것은 저작권법에 의한 법적 책임 을 물을 수 있습니다. 본 콘텐츠의 레이아웃 및 편집에 대한 저작권 침해 행위 또한 금지하고 있습니다. 영어I 지학사(신상근) 2과 예상문제 2회 - 객관식(선다형) 1. 주관식 2. ①, ② 3. ⑤ 4. ④ 5. ③ 6. 주관식 7. 주관식 8. 주관식 9. ⑤ 10. ③ 11. 주관식 12. ② 13. ⑤ 14. ① 15. ④ 16. ④ 17. ②

W: Hello, everyone! I’m Jenny, your host for Jenny’s
Creative Art Class. This week, we’ll be creating
self-portraits
like
Arcimboldo.
Giuseppe
Arcimboldo was an Italian painter born in 1526.
He is famous for painting his imaginative
portraits (A)[uses / using] the images of various
objects, such as fruits, vegetables, flowers, fish,
and books. In this lesson, we’ll explore some of
Arcimboldo’s
paintings
to
understand
his
distinctive style. Then, we’ll apply these insights
to create our self-portraits using the images of
various objects, following Arcimboldo’s style.
However, remember (B)[that / what] your task is
not to imitate his paintings but to tap into your
own imagination and creativity. Are you ready
to get started? I wonder how (C)[fascinating /
fascinated] your work would be. Let your
creativity shine!
(A)           (B)           (C)
choices: usingwhat  fascinated
useswhat  fascinating
usingthat  fascinated
usesthat  fascinating
usingthat  fascinating
solution: (A) 완전한 절(He ~ portraits)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 분사 구문을 이루는 현재분사 using이 적절하다. (B) 완전한 절(your task ~ creativity)을 이끌어 동사 remember 의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌어야 하므로 명사절 접 속사 that이 적절하다. body:
If you want to have good ideas, you must have
numerous ideas. Traditionally, people ⓐfollow the
saying that they prefer “quality over quantity.”
However, in the case of ideas, quantity and quality
are equally important. Highly creative individuals do
not actually produce better ideas than average
ones. Instead, they produce more ideas. Their
increased idea ⓑoutput means that they are more
likely to ⓒhit on something brilliant.
An excellent example is Pablo Picasso. Picasso is
famous for a handful of artworks. However, few
people realize that Picasso’s portfolio includes 2,800
ceramics, 1,800 paintings, 1,200 sculptures, and
more than 12,000 drawings. Again, only a fraction
of
them
became
famous.
Likewise,
Mozart
composed over 600 pieces before his death at age
35, only a handful of which are recognized as
particularly creative. Einstein also had more than
248 publications, but many of them didn’t have
much impact. The lesson here is to produce a large
volume of work. This way, you have more of a
ⓓchance that one or two will be outstanding. Just
pour out whatever ⓔcomes to mind and separate
the gems from the rocks.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

<보기>
ⓐfollow: to happen or do something after
something else
ⓑoutput: the amount of goods or work produced
by a person, machine, factory etc
ⓒhit on: to have an idea or discover something
suddenly or unexpectedly
ⓓchance: a time or situation which you can use
to do something that you want to do
ⓔcome to mind: to suddenly or immediately think
of something
solution: ⓐ (충고·지침 등을) 따르다: 다른 어떤 것 이후에 일어나거나 어떤 것을 하다(→to do something in the way that someone has told or advised you to do it(누군가가 당신에게 그것을 하라고 말했거나 조언한 방식대로 무언가를 하다)) ⓓ 가능성: 당신이 원하는 무언가를 하기 위해 사용할 수 있는 시간이나 상황(→the possibility that something will happen, especially something you want(특히 당신이 원하는 무언가가 일어날 가능성))

(A) Conventional wisdom suggests that quality is
more important than quantity, but this doesn't
apply to creativity. (T/F)
(B) The secret of creative geniuses is not that
they have better ideas, but that they produce
more ideas. (T/F)

almost all of their works become highly
successful and famous. (T/F)
(D) Einstein's case shows that even great geniuses
create many works that don‘t have a significant
impact. (T/F)

generate as many ideas as possible and then
select the best ones. (T/F)

(T) (일치) (C) 피카소와 모차르트 같은 역사적 거장들은 그들의 작품 거 의 전부가 매우 성공적이고 유명해지는 것을 보았다. (→피카 소와 모차르트의 작품 중 오직 극히 일부만이 유명해졌다고 했다.) (F) (불일치) (D) 아인슈타인의 사례는 위대한 천재들조차도 큰 영향을 갖지 못한 많은 작품들을 만들어 낸다는 것을 보여 준다. (T) (일치) (E) 뛰어난 아이디어를 찾기 위해서는 가능한 한 많은 아이디 어를 만들어 낸 뒤 그중에서 가장 좋은 것을 선택하는 것이 효과적이다. (T) (일치)

body:
Don’t Rush
We are frequently ⓐtelling that procrastination is
our worst enemy. Almost every self-help book
describes successful people as being those ⓑwho
can (A)[overcome / enjoy] procrastination. However,
several moments of genius have stemmed from
procrastination. Great originals know how to utilize
procrastination
as
a
strategy
in
their
idea
production. Procrastination (B)[promotes / impedes]
gradual progress rather than rapid progress, which
ⓒleaves your brain open to a wider range of ideas.
While
procrastination
may
be
the
enemy
of
productivity, it can be a resource for creativity.
Few people know that Leonardo da Vinci was a
chronic procrastinator. It took him 16 years to
complete the Mona Lisa. Some of the things that
took his attention away from work, like learning
optics, transformed ⓓthe way how he modeled
light and made him into a much better painter.
What about Martin Luther King, Jr.? The original
script of his speech, believe it or not, didn’t contain
the words “I have a dream.” The night before the
biggest speech of his life, he was up past 3 a.m.
rewriting his script. He was sitting in the audience
waiting for his turn to go onto the stage and still
writing notes on his script. After he got on stage,
11 minutes in, he heard Mahalia Jackson, his favorite
singer, cry out: “Tell them about the dream, Martin.”
Encouraged by a shout from the audience, he drew
upon some of his past talks, and the result became
the landmark speech “I have a dream.” By ⓔdelaying
the task of finalizing the speech until the very last
minute, he left himself open to the widest range of
possible ideas. The text wasn’t (C)[fixed / variable],
and he had the freedom to improvise.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)           (C)
choices: overcome      promotesfixed
enjoy  promotesfixed
overcome  promotesvariable
enjoy  impedesfixed
overcome  impedesvariable
solution: (A) 앞 문장에서 미루는 습관이 우리의 최악의 적이라는 말을 자주 듣는다고 했으므로, 성공한 사람들은 이러한 습관을 '극 복하는' 사람으로 묘사되는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 overcome (극복하다)이 적절하다. (B) 콤마(,) 뒤 절에서 뇌를 더 넓은 범위의 아이디어에 열려 있게 한다고 했으므로, 점진적인 진보를 ‘촉진’한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 promotes(촉진하다)가 적절하다. (C) 마지막 순간까지 원고 완성을 미룸으로써 아이디어의 가능 성을 열어두었다고 했으므로 연설문이 아직 ‘정해진‘ 상태가 아 니었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 fixed(정해진)가 적절하다.

body:
We often read stories about extremely intelligent,
gifted children. We might see an elementary school
student who can play the most difficult classical
music, a young boy who can do complicated math
in his head, or a little girl who can get into a
famous university before her 13th birthday. The
surprising thing, though, is ⓐwhat these children
aren’t usually very successful as adults.
Some people might explain this by assuming
ⓑwhich these extremely gifted young people have
poor social skills or low emotional intelligence.
(A)____________,
these
gifted
children
are
too
awkward, strange, and naive ⓒsucceeding in the
normal world. However, this theory is almost
certainly wrong. Extremely gifted children usually
have normal social skills and most of them are
comfortable going to parties, talking with friends,
and dealing with bosses or customers.
Instead, ⓓit seems to hold them back is their way
of learning. All the time a gifted child spends
memorizing Mozart is time he can’t spend learning
how to compose music himself. All the time an
extremely intelligent child spends studying for
university tests is time she can’t spend learning how
to think independently. In summary, these children
tend to spend all of their time memorizing old
ideas and skills but very little time ⓔcome up with
new ideas or skills. This, unfortunately, is what most
education encourages students to do.
According to many researchers, the skills that make
someone a child prodigy simply aren’t the same
skills that make an adult genius. This is because the
primary skill adult geniuses need is the ability to
make new connections, create new ideas, and see
new solutions to difficult problems. (B)____________,
child prodigies excel at doing the opposite — they
become exceptionally good at doing problems that
have already been solved, playing music that’s
already been written, and copying techniques that
have already been developed. Practice makes perfect,
but it doesn’t make “new.” Child prodigies who want
to become adult geniuses, therefore, have to reinvent
themselves before they can become innovators.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞게 고쳐 쓰지못한 것은?
choices: ⓐ: what → that
ⓑ: which → what
ⓒ: succeeding → to succeed
ⓓ: it → what
ⓔ: come → coming
solution: ⓑ which → that (완전한 절(these ~ emotional intelligence)을 이끌어 동명사 assuming의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌어야 하므로 which를 what이 아니라 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)

(B)
choices: NeverthelessIn short
In additionHowever
In other wordsAs a result

solution: (A) 어떤 사람들은 재능 있는 아이들이 서툰 대인 관계나 낮은 정 서 지능을 가지고 있다고 가정한다는 내용의 앞 문장을 뒷 문 장에서 ‘이 재능 있는 아이들은 평범한 세계에서 성공하기에는 너무 서툴고, 이상하고, 순진하다는 것이다.’라는 같은 내용이지 만 다른 말로 풀어서 한 번 더 설명하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 In other words(다시 말해서), That is(다시 말해서)가 적절하다. (B) 앞 문장에서 성인 천재에게 필요한 새로운 연결, 독창적 아이 디어와 같은 기술들을 설명하고, 빈칸 뒤에서 재능 있는 아이 들이 그와 정반대인 이미 해결된 문제나 이미 쓰인 음악을 복제 하는 데만 능숙하다는 부정적인 내용이 이어지므로 빈칸에는 부정적인 상황을 연결하는 Unfortunately(안타깝게도) 또는 앞 문장과 상반된 내용을 연결하는 However(그러나)가 적절하다.

The hallmark of originality is rejecting the default
and finding out if a better option exists. (A)일을 다
르게 하는 여러분의 능력, 일이 진행되는 방식에 의문
을 제기하고 개선하는 능력이 여러분을 창의적이고 다
르게 만드는 것이다. Your Internet browser is a pain?
Change it! You don’t like the system? Say so! You
have a new idea? Try it! You see a better way of
doing things? Test it! Most people won’t take any
risk. They’ll just stick with what they know, thinking
it’ll be good enough. But if you think that you can
change things, then your originality and your
creativity could make a big difference in the end.
The founders of an online eyewear company, for
instance, couldn’t understand why it was so hard to
find an affordable pair of glasses. They thought the
problem was interesting, so they conducted some
research.
They
found
that
just
one
company
dominated 80% of the market. As a result, they
created a company that no one expected to thrive.
Instead of depending on only physical stores where

created a business where you could simply order

business model, they were able to offer glasses that

time a customer purchased glasses from them,

Francis Kéré, a winner of the Pritzker Prize, was born
in Burkina Faso, one of the poorest countries in Africa.
The region in Africa (A)[which / where] he grew up
didn’t have any electricity or running water. When he
was seven, he had to move 13 km away to attend
school. He made history in his village as its first
student ever. The conditions of the school he attended
were very ⓐ[good / poor]. The classroom, hastily
(B)[constructing / constructed] from cement, was filled
with over a hundred children. With temperatures often
exceeding 40 degrees and without any form of lighting,
it was a ⓑ[challenging / favorable] environment for
learning. Although Kéré could have given up his
dreams, he remained determined to study.
While still a young student, he (C)[awarded / was
awarded] a scholarship to study carpentry in Germany.
He finished his high school studies in Germany and
went on to attend university there as well. Even though
he became a globally recognized architect in Germany,
he has not ⓒ[embraced / forgotten] his roots. His
architectural designs are deeply influenced by his love
for Africa and a profound sense of pride in his people.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: whereconstructed awarded
whereconstructing was awarded
whichconstructing awarded
whereconstructed was awarded
whichconstructed was awarded
solution: (A) 완전한 절(he grew up)을 이끌어 장소를 나타내는 선행사 The region in Africa를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다. (B) 주어 The classroom과 동사 was 사이에 이중 콤마(,)로 삽입되어 주어 The classroom을 부연 설명하는 분사구로, The classroom이 ‘지 어진’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미인 과거분사 constructed가 적절하다. (C) 주어 he에 이어지는 동사 자리로, he가 장학금을 ‘받는’ 대상이므 로 수동태(be+p.p.)인 was awarded가 적절하다. 참고로 동사 award는 ‘award+간접목적어+직접목적어(…에게 ~을 수여하다)’의 구조를 갖는 4형식 동사로, 두 개의 목적어를 취하기에 수동태(be awarded)로 전 환해도 뒤에 능동태의 '직접목적어‘였던 명사구가 그대로 남아있다.

Located in Burkina Faso’s third largest city, the Lycée
Schorge Secondary School is ⓐcomprised of nine
distinct modules. These modules house a collection of
classrooms and offices, all centered around a main
public courtyard. This design ensures privacy from the
main public area while simultaneously sheltering and
ⓑprotects the courtyard against wind and dust.
Kéré tackled the problem of limited resources
during the building’s construction by using materials
that ⓒwere easy to find in the region in the same
manner as before. First of all, he built the walls of
the
building
using
bricks
made
from
readily
available stone in the region. These bricks help cool
the building by absorbing intense daytime heat and
later releasing it during the night.
As with many other buildings, an overhanging roof
protects the brick walls from the harsh African sun
while also ⓓfacilitating air circulation below. To
capture fresh air and let hot air escape, Kéré also
added wind towers on top of each classroom. The
school is surrounded by a screen made from
fast-growing local eucalyptus trees. This screen
provides more than just protection against dust and
wind. It also creates casual spaces where students
can gather as they wait for their classes ⓔto begin.

body:
Serpentine Pavilion
Over time Kéré’s work has expanded well beyond
Africa. It now includes temporary and permanent
structures in Denmark, Germany, Italy, Switzerland,
the UK, and the USA. Perhaps not too surprisingly,
his works outside of Africa are influenced by his
experiences in Gando.
(A) The pavilion’s roof, resembling the wide branches
of a tree, includes a transparent layer that
allows sunlight to spread into the pavilion
below. Visitors may enter the pavilion through
one of its four entrances and sit around the
central ring to look up at the sky.
(B) A perfect example is the colorful Serpentine
Pavilion in London. Since the year 2000, the
Serpentine Gallery in the UK has annually
invited distinguished architects from around the
world to design a pavilion, which provides a
place of rest for visitors.
(C) In 2017, the honor was extended to Kéré.
Drawing inspiration from his hometown, where
locals would gather to work, converse, and

Serpentine Pavilion
Over time Kéré’s work has expanded well beyond
Africa. It now includes temporary and permanent
structures in Denmark, Germany, Italy, Switzerland,
the UK, and the USA. Perhaps not too surprisingly,
his works outside of Africa are influenced by his
experiences in Gando.
(A) The pavilion’s roof, resembling the wide branches
of a tree, includes a transparent layer that
allows sunlight to spread into the pavilion
below. Visitors may enter the pavilion through
one of its four entrances and sit around the
central ring to look up at the sky.
(B) A perfect example is the colorful Serpentine
Pavilion in London. Since the year 2000, the
Serpentine Gallery in the UK has annually
invited distinguished architects from around the
world to design a pavilion, which provides a
place of rest for visitors.
(C) In 2017, the honor was extended to Kéré.
Drawing inspiration from his hometown, where
locals would gather to work, converse, and
study beneath the shade of trees, he modeled
his design after a large tree.

Francis Kéré, a winner of the Pritzker Prize, was
born in Burkina Faso, one of the poorest countries
in Africa. The region in Africa where he grew up
didn’t have any electricity or running water. When
he was seven, he had to move 13 km away to
attend school. He made history in his village as its
first student ever. The conditions of the school he
attended were very poor. The classroom, hastily
constructed from cement, was filled with over a
hundred
children.
With
temperatures
often
exceeding 40 degrees and without any form of
lighting, it was a challenging environment for
learning. Although Kéré could have given up his
dreams, he remained determined to study.
While still a young student, he was awarded a
scholarship to study carpentry in Germany. He
finished his high school studies in Germany and
went on to attend university there as well. Even
though he became a globally recognized architect
in Germany, he has not forgotten his roots. His
architectural designs ___________________________________
and a profound sense of pride in his people.
choices: represent the tastes of wealthy and powerful people
mainly reflect his practical experiences in Germany
strictly follow the latest global architectural trends
prioritize modern aesthetics over traditional values
are deeply influenced by his love for Africa지학사(신상근) 3과
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Gando Primary School
For his first project, he managed to raise ＄30,000
to build an elementary school in his native village,
Gando. Instead of using more conventional modern
materials like concrete, glass, and steel, he chose to
use clay, embracing the traditional building methods
of Africa. He made bricks by mixing clay, a locally
available material, with 10% cement. This mixture
helps keep classrooms cool during hot weather.
(A)_____________, he used bricks with holes in them
to make the ceiling and built a high roof using a
contemporary architectural system to let hot air
escape. The large overhanging roof provides shade
and protects the clay bricks from heavy rain.
Traditionally, members of a whole village work
together to build and repair homes in rural Burkina
Faso. In keeping with this cultural practice, Kéré
encouraged the villagers of Gando to take part in
the construction process. His objective was for them
to make the place on their own. Children gathered
stones for the school foundation and women
brought water for brick manufacturing. He also
trained the young members of the village and then
they collaborated on the construction. These trained
workers have since used these new skills to build
schools
and
houses
in
other
communities.
(B)_____________, he made all the architectural plans
for the school construction available to anyone in
the village, which made it easier for two nearby
villages to build their own schools. Thanks to the
success of this project, the number of students
increased from 120 to a remarkable 700.

body:
We are frequently told that procrastination is our
worst enemy. ㉠거의 모든 자기계발서는 성공한 사람들
을 미루는 습관을 극복할 수 있는 사람들로 묘사한다.
However, several moments of genius have stemmed
from procrastination. Great originals know how to
utilize procrastination as a strategy in their idea
production.
Procrastination
encourages
gradual
progress rather than rapid progress, which leaves
your brain open to a wider range of ideas. While
procrastination may be the enemy of productivity, it
can be a resource for creativity.
Few people know that Leonardo da Vinci was a
chronic procrastinator. It took him 16 years to
complete the Mona Lisa. Some of the things that
took his attention away from work, like learning
optics, transformed the way he modeled light and
made him into a much better painter.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?

(A) Self-help books usually define success as the
ability to defeat the urge to delay tasks. (T/F)
(B) A wider variety of ideas can be accessed by
the brain when progress is slowed through
procrastination. (T/F)
(C) Although it harms efficiency, delaying work serves
as a helpful resource for creative thought. (T/F)
(D) The act of procrastination was observed in
Leonardo da Vinci only during his production
of the Mona Lisa. (T/F)
(E) Leonardo da Vinci’s artistic growth was limited as
his attention was diverted to studying optics. (T/F)

What about Martin Luther King, Jr.? The original
script of his speech, believe it or not, didn’t contain
the words “I have a dream.” The night before the
biggest speech of his life, he was up past 3 a.m.
rewriting his script. (A)그는 무대에 오를 자신의 차례
를 기다리며 관중석에 앉아 있었고, 여전히 자신의 원
고에 메모를 쓰고 있었다. After he got on stage, 11
minutes in, he heard Mahalia Jackson, his favorite
singer, cry out: “Tell them about the dream, Martin.”
(B)____________ by a shout from the audience, he
drew upon some of his past talks, and the result
became the landmark speech “I have a dream.” By
delaying the task of finalizing the speech until the
very last minute, he left himself open to the widest
range of possible ideas. The text wasn’t set in
stone, and he had the (C)____________ to improvise.

윗글의 빈칸 (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(B)                    (C)
choices: Encouragedconstraint
Inspiredflexibility
Deterredspontaneity
Intimidatedfreedom
Motivatedrestriction
solution: (B) 그의 연설문의 원래 원고에는 ‘나에게는 꿈이 있습니다.’라 는 말이 들어 있지 않았으나, 이후 꿈에 대해 말해달라는 관객 의 외침에 의해, ‘나에게는 꿈이 있습니다.’라는 획기적인 연설 이 되었다고 언급하고 있으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 Encouraged(고무된), Inspired(영감은 받은), Motivated(동 기부여 된)가 적절하다. (C) 마지막 순간까지 원고를 확정 짓지 않았기 때문에 Martin Luther King, Jr.는 즉흥적으로 연설을 할 수 있었다. 따라서 빈 칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 flexibility(유연함), spontaneity (즉흥성), freedom(자유)이 적절하다. 지학사(신상근) 5과

and ⓐfinds out if a better option exists. Your
ability to do things differently, to question and
ⓑrefine the way things work is what makes you
creative and different. Your Internet browser is a
pain? Change it! You don’t like the system? Say so!
You have a new idea? Try it! You see a better way
of doing things? Test it! Most people won’t take
any risk. They’ll just stick with what they know,
thinking it’ll be good enough. But if you think that
you can change things, then your originality and your
creativity could make a big difference in the end.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 독창성은 기존 방식에 의문을 제기하고 더 나은 방법을 찾으 려는 태도에서 시작되고, 기존의 것을 고수하지 않고 상황을 바꿀 수 있다고 생각한다면, 독창성과 창의성이 큰 변화를 만 들어낼 수 있다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 앞서 제시된 주장을 뒷받침 하기 위해 한 온라인 안경 회사의 창업자들의 사례를 처음 소 개하며, 왜 저렴한 안경을 찾는 것이 그렇게 어려운지 이해할 수 없다는 점을 문제를 제기한 (C), 그 문제를 the problem(그 문제)으로 이어 받아 흥미롭게 여겨 조사를 수행했다는 내용의 (A), (A)의 마지막 문장에서 조사 결과 한 회사가 시장을 독점 하는 것을 문제의 원인으로 제시한 뒤 As a result(그 결과)로 연결하여 독점 시장에 뛰어들어 아무도 성공할 것이라 예상하지 않았던 회사를 설립했다는 (B)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

If you want to have good ideas, you must have
numerous ideas. Traditionally, people follow the saying
that they prefer “quality over quantity.” However, in
the case of ideas, quantity and quality are equally
important. Highly creative individuals do not actually
produce better ideas than average ones. Instead,
they produce more ideas. Their increased idea
output means that _________________________________.
choices: they are more likely to hit on something brilliant
their brilliance stems from their innate talent ratherthan trial and error
they can produce successful ideas without havingto invest much time
the success of their ideas is primarily shaped byexternal environments
they should focus on the perfection of eachidea rather than the total number
solution: 좋은 아이디어를 얻기 위해서는 많은 아이디어를 가져야 하며, 창의적인 사람들 역시 처음부터 더 뛰어난 아이디어를 내는 것이 아니라 단지 더 많은 아이디어를 생산한다고 했으므로 그들의 증가된 아이디어 생산량은 결국 더 뛰어난 아이디어를 발견할 가능성이 높다는 의미로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. 따 라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은 ❶ ‘그들이 훌륭한 무언가를 떠올릴 가능성이 더 크다’이다. 지학사(신상근) 5과

We often read stories about extremely intelligent,
gifted children. We might see an elementary school
student who can play the most difficult classical
music, a young boy who can do complicated math
in his head, or a little girl who can get into a
famous university before her 13th birthday. The
surprising thing, though, is that these children aren’t
usually very successful as adults.
Some people might explain this by assuming that
these extremely gifted young people have poor
social skills or low emotional intelligence. In other
words, these gifted children are too awkward,
strange, and naive to succeed in the normal world.
However, this theory is almost certainly wrong.
Extremely gifted children usually have normal social
skills and most of them are comfortable going to
parties, talking with friends, and dealing with bosses
or customers.
(A)____________ the common belief that gifted
children (B)____________ in adulthood due to their
poor interpersonal relations, they actually have no
(C)____________ functioning socially as well as their
peers.
(A)               (B)
(C)
choices: In contrast to     fall behind advantage of
Consistent with   succeed trouble in
Contrary to    underachieve difficulty in
In line with    struggle facility for
Opposed to    prosper challenge of

body:
Instead, what seems to hold them back is their
way of learning. All the time a gifted child spends
memorizing Mozart is time he can’t spend learning
how to compose music himself. All the time an
extremely intelligent child spends studying for
university tests is time she can’t spend learning how
to think independently. In summary, these children
tend to spend all of their time memorizing old
ideas and skills but very little time coming up with
new ideas or skills. This, unfortunately, is what most
education encourages students to do.
According to many researchers, the skills that
make someone a child prodigy simply aren’t the
same skills that make an adult genius. This is
because the primary skill adult geniuses need is the
ability to make new connections, create new ideas,
and
see
new
solutions
to
difficult
problems.
Unfortunately, child prodigies excel at doing the
opposite — they
become
exceptionally
good
at
doing problems that have already been solved,
playing music that’s already been written, and
copying
techniques
that
have
already
been
developed. Practice makes perfect, but it doesn’t
make “new.” Child prodigies who want to become
adult
geniuses,
therefore,
have
to
reinvent
themselves before they can become innovators.

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: What is the primary factor that prevents giftedchildren from becoming successful adult geniuses?
How does the time spent on memorization affectgifted children's development of independentthinking?
What is the reason for differentiating thecurriculum between gifted children and averagestudents?
What are the specific skills required for an adultgenius that child prodigies often lack?
Why is 'practice' alone insufficient for childprodigies who dream of becoming innovators?
solution: 재능 있는 아이들은 오래된 아이디어와 기술을 암기하는 데 그들의 모든 시간을 쓰지만 새로운 아이디어나 기술을 생각해 내는 데는 거의 시간을 할애하지 않는 경향이 있으며, 대부분 의 교육이 이런 방식을 학생들에게 장려한다고 했으므로 재능 있는 아이들과 일반 학생들의 교육 방식이 차별화되었다고 볼 수 없다. 따라서 ❸ ‘재능 있는 아이들과 일반 학생들 사이에 서 교육과정을 차별화하는 이유는 무엇인가?’는 답할 수 없는 질문이다.
